title: 500.29 Artificial Intelligence Based Optical Coherence Tomography Comparison of Plaque Characteristics and DNA Repair Activity in Patients with CAD
abstract:
BACKGROUND Previous CAD studies have demonstrated associations between DNA repair activity (which may be measured in vitro using DNA ligase assays), telomere length, and atherosclerosis. We intend to explore the relationship between atherosclerotic plaque characteristics and DNA ligase activity.

METHODS 49 subjects (25 stable angina, 24 NSTEMI) were included from the DECODE study (ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT02335086). OCT imaging of the culprit vessel was performed and it was analyzed using OCTplus, an artificial intelligence-based software evaluating for the area (in mm²) of calcium, cholesterol crystal, fibrous tissue, lipid and macrophage. DNA ligase activity was measured in blood mononuclear cells using microplate-based assays and was available for 38 patients. Continuous variables are reported as mean ± SD. Comparisons of means between groups were performed with Student T tests. A p-value of < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.

RESULTS Baseline characteristics were similar between stable angina and NSTEMI patients. Grouping patients based on median DNA ligase activity revealed no significant differences in plaque characteristics in both patient cohorts. Calcification was 66.96 % larger in the high ligase activity group (0.53 ± 0.48 mm²) vs low ligase assay (0.18 ± 0.15 mm²), absolute difference of 0.35 ± 0.33 mm², p = 0.053. See table.

CONCLUSIONS We found a trend toward larger calcium content in the stable angina group with high ligase activity. We previously found that expression of DNA damage response pathway genes in patients with stable angina was strongly associated with fibrocalcific plaques.
